title: The logical set of Gaussian states under the stabilizer subsystem decomposition
authors: Santiago Zamora, Kaustav Chatterjee, Ulrik Lund Andersen, Thiago Lucena de Macedo Guedes, Jonatan Bohr Brask, A. de Oliveira Junior, Rafael Chaves
abstract: Universal quantum computation requires non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable systems and non-stabilizerness in discrete-variable systems. Yet, mapping a Gaussian state into the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill logical subspace can yield a logical qubit with non-stabilizer resources. To understand how the continuous-variable structure determines logical resources, we characterize the image of single-mode Gaussian states under the corresponding extraction channel, known as the stabilizer subsystem decomposition. Specifically, we derive series expressions for the logical Bloch vector and characterize the resulting reachable set, enabling an analytical treatment of the robustness of magic of the logical states. We then turn this geometric framework into a certification tool: by mapping a discrete-variable qubit witness to a continuous-variable squeezing witness, we obtain lower bounds on the squeezing of prepared states. We also show that ensembles of Gaussian states can violate both stabilizer and classical bounds. Violation of the stabilizer bound certifies the relational resource known as "set-magic," while violation of the classical bound enables the certification of cryptographic randomness at moderate squeezing.
summary: This paper analyzes how Gaussian quantum states behave when encoded into the GKP logical subspace using the stabilizer subsystem decomposition. The authors derive geometric bounds showing that these states can exhibit non-stabilizer properties, which they use to create novel certification tools. These tools allow for quantifying resources like 'set-magic' and certifying cryptographic randomness based on measurable squeezing levels.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the logical set of Gaussian states when mapped into the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) logical subspace via the stabilizer subsystem decomposition (SSD). It aims to derive practical certification tools based on this geometric understanding.
main_result: The logical image of single-mode Gaussian states can violate the stabilizer bound, certifying a resource called "set-magic." Furthermore, violating the classical bound allows for the certification of cryptographic randomness at moderate squeezing levels.
method: The authors derive exact series expressions for the logical Bloch vector components and analyze the resulting reachable set geometry. They apply this framework by mapping discrete-variable witnesses to continuous-variable squeezing witnesses.
model_or_system: The study focuses on continuous-variable (CV) bosonic systems, specifically single-mode Gaussian states, and their behavior when subjected to the GKP logical subspace extraction channel (SSD).
key_observables: Logical Bloch vector components (X, Y, Z), robustness of magic $R(1)(ho_L)$, and the conditional min-entropy $H_{\min}(B|E)$.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($r$), displacement ($\mathbf{d}$), and the time/witness parameter ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ideal GKP error correction and the faithful SSD extraction channel. Approximations are used for the maximum robustness and worst-case entropy calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the XZ projections of the logical state set, comparing the exact boundary to leading-harmonic approximations, and show the relationship between various bounds and the certified min-entropy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing the logical set geometry, deriving series expressions for the Bloch vector, and establishing the relationship between Gaussian inputs and the stabilizer polytope. It then applies this geometry to develop certification tools for set-magic and cryptographic randomness.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical framework connecting continuous-variable resource theory (squeezing, Gaussian states) to discrete-variable quantum information concepts (stabilizer codes, magic states, randomness certification).
